battle.name: 建康之戰
battle.brief: 474年，南齊內政崩壞之際北魏再度南下，兵鋒直指壽陽至瓜步一線，南齊倚建康西北的瓜步壘與弩砲拒守，魏軍終不得渡江。卡面羅馬重步兵只作對照：羅馬靠補充兵源與補給線維持重步兵，南齊靠建康倉儲與運河、北魏靠軍鎮屯田維持遠征兵，誰的補給線撐得住，誰就守得住江防。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 建康之戰（474年）是南北朝前期南齊與北魏在淮水一線正面碰撞的一場戰役，記載多散見於《魏書》顯祖紀與《南齊書》諸列傳。南齊一方以建康為中樞：後廢帝在位時，禁旅以中軍為核心，宿衛由領軍將軍、護軍將軍分領，宮禁與京畿要害另置直閣與武騎常侍一類近衛；外軍則來自揚州、南徐州、徐州、益州等州郡，刺史與太守徵發州兵、鎮兵、郡兵以及縣邑丁役，兵糧由建康的倉儲沿揚子江、秦淮河與運河分撥至前線，指揮則出自尚書令、中書令與給事中，詔書與中旨下到各軍行營。北魏一方以平城與洛陽為兩處中樞：獻文帝拓跋弘在位時，軍隊仍以拓跋部落的騎兵為骨幹，漢人郡縣兵與軍鎮兵分列其外，州鎮屯田所出之糧經泗水、淮水轉運至南征大軍的營地，兵權集中於都督大將軍與各路將領之手，邊線由壽陽、彭城一類的軍鎮據點配合游騎巡邏維持。兩國在淮水南北各有縱深：南齊倚長江與運河，北魏倚黃河與平原道路，因此這一線的打法不是一次會戰分出勝負，而是以據點、糧道與援軍到來的快慢互相消耗。
countriesEn: The Battle of Jiankang (474) was a direct collision between Southern Qi and Northern Wei on the Huai River line during the early Northern and Southern Dynasties, and its records are scattered across the Weishu account of Emperor Xianwen and the biographical sections of the Nanzhi shu. On the Southern Qi side, Jiankang was the hub: under the Later Emperor the palace guard was built around the Central Army, with the Lingjun jiangjun and the Hujun jiangjun holding separate commands, while the imperial city and the capital district were watched by closer guards such as the Zhige and the wuqi changshi. The field forces were drawn from the provinces of Yang, Southern Xu, Xu and Yi, where governors and commandery administrators mustered zhou troops, garrison troops, commandery troops and county labour, and the grain for them was moved out of the granaries of Jiankang along the Yangzi, the Qinhuai River and the canal network. Orders went out from the Shangshu ling, the Zhongshu ling and the Jishizhong, as imperial edicts and inner-court instructions to the various field camps. On the Northern Wei side there were two centres, Pingcheng and Luoyang: under Emperor Xianwen, Tuoba clan cavalry remained the backbone of the army, with Han Chinese commandery and garrison troops arrayed around them, and the grain produced by the state farms of the garrisons was carried down the Si and Huai rivers to the camps of the invading army. Command was concentrated in the dudu da jiangjun and the commanders of each column, and the front was held by military towns such as Shouyang and Pengcheng together with roving patrols. Each side had depth behind it: Southern Qi relied on the Yangzi and the canals, Northern Wei on the Yellow River and the plain roads. The fighting on this line was therefore not a single decisive battle but a running contest in which strongpoints, supply routes and the speed with which reinforcements arrived wore each other down.
people: 北魏一方的主導者是獻文帝拓跋弘（451年至476年在位）。他在皇興元年受禪稱帝之前已以攝政身份經營北方軍政，在劉宋北伐於彭城、青州一線受挫之後接掌兵權；在位期間他把南征當成長線的國策，先有正面的渡淮攻勢，其後因風疾傳位給孝文帝拓跋宏，拓跋宏在承明年間仍延續了這條戰線。宗室之中，廣平公拓跋英是這段時期最吃重的統帥，他坐鎮河北、總攝漢地軍務，承明年間數次率大軍東出，直趨淮北；其後他奉命與南朝議和，卻在接境交涉之地因急病暴卒，北魏內部隨之一片混亂，齊魏之間的僵局也就此收束。南齊一方最先決定局面的，是當時還只是中軍高層的蕭道成：他以整軍的名義整頓禁軍，在南齊後廢帝誅戮將相、朝政崩壞的亂局裡逐步掌握兵權，先後廢去後廢帝、擁立順帝，最終在建元元年受禪，建立南齊。前線的實際作戰者則是陳顯達、沈文圭、張保、戴僧靜等人：陳顯達以鎮守徐州、淮南的經驗應付壽陽方向的攻防，沈文圭與張保、戴僧靜在瓜步一線築壘拒騎，把魏軍擋在長江北岸；戴法興一類權臣則在宮中推動了對後廢帝的清洗，使軍政中樞在戰事正熾的時候反而換了一次人事，這對遠在前線的將領與運糧的民夫都是直接的影響。
peopleEn: On the Northern Wei side the driving figure was Emperor Xianwen of Northern Wei, Tuoba Hong (451-476). Before he took the throne as emperor in the first year of Huangxing he had already run the northern military and civil administration as regent, and he took charge of military power after the Liu Song northern thrusts toward Pengcheng and Qingzhou had been broken. He treated southern campaigns as a long-term policy of the state, mounting direct offensives across the Huai; later, afflicted by a paralytic illness, he handed the throne to Emperor Xiaowen, Tuoba Hong, who carried the same war policy forward in the Chengming years. Among the imperial clan, the Duke of Guangping, Tuoba Ying, was the heaviest single commander of the period: he held the northern provinces and general command over the Han territories, and in the Chengming years led armies eastward more than once toward the Huai. He was later sent to negotiate a truce with the southern court, and died suddenly of illness at the border meeting place, and the north was thrown into confusion, and with that the Qi-Wei stalemate closed. On the Southern Qi side, the man who first decided the outcome was Xiao Daocheng, then only a senior officer of the Central Army: he reorganised the palace guard in the guise of restoring military discipline, and in the collapse of the Later Emperor's reign, with its slaughter of generals and ministers and its ruinous government, he progressively took command of the armed forces, deposed the Later Emperor, set up Prince Zhun, and finally received the abdication in the first year of Jianyuan to found Southern Qi. The men who actually fought were Chen Xianda, Shen Wengui, Zhang Bao and Dai Sengjing: Chen Xianda handled the defence of Shouyang and the Huai with his experience in the northern marches, while Shen Wengui, Zhang Bao and Dai Sengjing built redoubts at Guabu to hold the cavalry off the north bank of the river. Ministers of the Dai faction such as Dai Faxing pushed the purge of the Later Emperor inside the palace, so that the centre of command was reshuffled even while the fighting was at its fiercest, which bore directly on the generals at the front and on the civilians moving grain.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是羅馬重步兵，配分段鎧甲與矩盾，持短劍與標槍，它在戰役裡的位置需要說明：它並沒有出現在淮水兩岸，它是拿來當量尺用的。羅馬重步兵的戰力從來不在甲胄本身，而在補充兵源與補給線；只要後方能持續補上合格的老兵與兵員，前線的盾牆就能維持，一旦糧道被切斷，盾牆就會在幾日之內散掉。對照南齊一方的裝備：禁旅與宿衛甲士穿札甲、戴兜鍪，執大盾與長槊，並配擲張弩與床子弩，州郡鄉兵則以環首刀、矛與木盾為主；對照北魏一方：拓跋部落的騎兵披掛人馬甲而以長槊、環首刀作主武器，鎮兵步卒穿札甲、結盾陣，攻城靠撞車與雲梯，野戰佈陣則用排車與拒馬阻騎。真正決定江防成敗的，是那批能反覆射擊的弩手與阻擋騎兵的拒馬、壕塹，而不是任何一件重裝備。羅馬重步兵還提供第二個教訓：重步兵必須有可以退守的據點與可以依賴的糧道。南齊的瓜步壘正扮演了這個角色，壘後的運河把建康的糧食一批批送到前線；北魏的軍鎮屯田則是同樣性質的東西，只是方向與羅馬相反，是從北方把糧食往南運。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman legionary, wearing segmented armour and carrying the rectangular scutum with a gladius and a pilum, and its place in this battle has to be stated plainly: it was never present on either bank of the Huai, and it is offered as a standard of comparison. A Roman legionary's strength never lay in the armour itself but in the replenishment of manpower and in the supply line: as long as the rear could keep sending up trained veterans and replacements, the shield wall could be held; once the grain route was cut, that wall came apart within a few days. Set against the equipment of Southern Qi: the guards and palace troops wore lamellar armour and helmets and carried large shields and long spears, with tension bows and bed crossbows assigned to them, while the provincial levies were armed mainly with ring-pommelled sabres, spears and wooden shields. Set against Northern Wei: the Tuoba clan cavalry wore armour for man and horse and fought with long spears and ring-pommelled sabres; the garrison infantry wore lamellar armour and formed up in shields, with battering rams and siege ladders for assaults, and wagons and barriers to break up charges in the field. What actually decided the defence of the river was the line of repeating crossbowmen and the pits and barriers that stopped cavalry, not any particular piece of heavy equipment. The second lesson of the Roman legionary is that heavy infantry must have a place to fall back on and a grain road to depend on. The Guabu redoubt played exactly that role for Southern Qi, and the canal behind it carried the food of Jiankang forward in batches; the military farms of Northern Wei served the same function, only in the opposite direction, moving grain south from the north.
tactics: 南齊與北魏在淮水一線的作戰，樣式與羅馬兵營的思路並無相似，卻有同一個毛病：都要靠地勢換時間。北魏的野戰以騎兵為主，標準打法是避開正面深溝高壘的城池，帶輕騎越過淮水去切對方的糧道與鄉鎮，逼迫對方分兵，然後再集中兵攻打援；若對方把兵都壓在城上，就轉為長久的圍城與斷糧，等城內存糧見底。北魏在壽陽一線用過的正是這一套：圍城、絕糧、策反城內的漢人守將，同時留一部騎兵在城外游弋，攔截南方的援軍，戰事因此拖成數月。南齊的應對分兩層：外層由陳顯達一類宿將據壽陽、盱眙、彭城等要塞，深溝高壘，弓弩居高臨下拒騎；內層則在瓜步一線沿江築壘，挖壕、設榔，把木柵與拒馬擺在騎兵衝得到的距離之外，逼魏軍下馬攻柵。弩手在壘後連續射擊，魏騎若強衝柵陣，就會在江岸前失去速度與隊形。水面同樣是防線的一環，南齊以揚子江的水師與江岸步軍互相策應，魏軍沒有可用的水師，就只能望江而止，屯兵北岸。撤退與追擊同樣屬於戰術的一部分：魏軍一旦糧盡或遇上疫病，就必須整隊北撤，齊軍這時以騎兵與輕兵尾隨追擊，切斷浮橋與渡口，逼對方丟掉輜重；反過來，齊軍每次派大軍西出，補給線拉得越長，被魏騎切斷的風險就越大，所以齊的用兵一直避免深入淮北太深。
tacticsEn: The way Southern Qi and Northern Wei fought along the Huai bears no resemblance to the drill of a Roman camp, but it suffers from the same fault: both sides tried to buy time with ground. Northern Wei fought mainly with cavalry in the field. The standard method was to avoid cities protected by deep ditches and high redoubts, to send light horse across the Huai to cut the enemy's supply roads and villages, to force the enemy to divide, and then to concentrate for an ambush on the relieving column; if the enemy massed everything behind the walls, the siege turned into a long blockade and starvation, waiting for the stores inside the city to run out. That is exactly what was used at Shouyang: encircling the city, cutting the grain road, working on the Han Chinese commanders inside, while a detachment of cavalry patrolled outside to intercept relief from the south, so that the business dragged on for months. Southern Qi answered on two levels. On the outer level, veterans such as Chen Xianda held Shouyang, Xuyi and Pengcheng, cutting deep ditches and raising high works so that bows and crossbows could shoot down at cavalry from above. On the inner level, the line at Guabu built redoubts along the river, dug ditches and set up stockades, placing wooden fences and barriers just beyond the distance a horseman could charge, forcing the Wei cavalry to dismount and attack the fence. The crossbowmen behind the works fired continuously, and a charge by Wei horse against the stockade would lose its speed and its order before it reached the bank. The river itself was a line of defence as well, with Southern Qi naval units on the Yangzi working in concert with the infantry on the bank; Wei had no usable fleet and could only look at the river and stop, camped on the north shore. Withdrawal and pursuit were part of the art as well: once grain ran short or sickness appeared, the Wei army had to withdraw in order, and the Qi light horse would follow and cut the pontoon bridges and fords, forcing the enemy to abandon baggage; conversely, every time Qi sent a large army west the longer its supply line grew and the greater the risk of being cut, which is why Qi avoided pushing too deep into the country north of the Huai.
data: 可以落到數字上的部分並不多，以下幾項大致可靠。時間上，474年是南齊與北魏在淮水一線衝突再度升級的一年，此後北魏在承明元年至承明三年之間多次南征，478年兵鋒抵達瓜步，479年南齊由陳顯達收復壽陽，這一輪攻防才算收束；至於本戰確切的起訖月份，諸史記載多有缺略。地理上，前線大致落在淮水一線，往北可追到黃河故地；瓜步在長江北岸、建康城西北數十里，是江防的關鍵；壽陽在淮水之濱，位於今安徽壽縣一帶，扼南北水陸要道，位置比瓜步更內陸，也更難防守。距離上，北魏大軍自洛陽沿泗水、淮水東下，行程一千餘里；南齊的援軍由建康向西出發三百餘里才能接上瓜步，意味著齊方每一次調兵都要先付三百里的行軍成本。兵力上，遠征的魏軍以騎兵為主，古史常記十餘萬之眾，這類數字出自遠征者自己的誇張，較可信的量級是以萬計的騎兵加上數萬的步卒；南齊在瓜步與壽陽一線的前線部隊屬於數千至數萬的規模，京師中軍與各州兵則是後續梯隊。時間成本上，圍攻壽陽一類的戰事常拖數月，遠征軍的糧秣靠牛車沿運河與河道分批輸送，車隊的長度、渡口的控制與沿線徵發的速度，決定了遠征能走多遠。氣候同樣是變數：江淮一帶春夏多雨、疫病易行，450年太武帝南征與478年拓跋英抵瓜步的兩次遠征，都留下病卒與疲耗的記載，時節選錯，一次攻勢就會在不交戰的情況下自行崩解。
dataEn: Little of this can be pinned to exact numbers, but the following are broadly sound. In time, 474 was the year in which the clash on the Huai line was escalated again; Northern Wei campaigned south several times between the first and third years of Chengming, reached Guabu in 478, and in 479 Chen Xianda of Southern Qi retook Shouyang, which closed that round of offence and defence; as for the exact opening and closing months of the battle itself, the old records are largely missing. In geography, the front fell broadly on the line of the Huai, traceable northward to the old Yellow River country; Guabu lay on the north bank of the Yangzi, several dozen li north-west of the city of Jiankang, and was the hinge of the river defence; Shouyang stood on the Huai, in what is today Shou County in Anhui, commanding the land and water routes between north and south, further inland than Guabu and correspondingly harder to hold. In distance, the Wei host moved east from Luoyang along the Si and Huai rivers, a journey of something over a thousand li, while a Qi relief column had to march more than three hundred li west from Jiankang to reach Guabu, so that every Qi dispatch paid a march of three hundred li before the men arrived. In strength, the invading Wei army was cavalry-led, and the old histories habitually give figures of more than a hundred thousand; such numbers come from the exaggeration of the campaigns themselves, and the more credible order of magnitude is cavalry in the tens of thousands with infantry in the tens of thousands. The forward troops at Guabu and Shouyang numbered in the thousands, with the capital's Central Army and the provincial levies arriving as follow-up echelons. In time cost, sieges such as that of Shouyang commonly ran for months; the grain of a distant army moved in batches by ox-cart along the canals and watercourses, and the length of the wagon train, the control of the crossings and the speed of requisition along the route decided how far a campaign could go. Climate was a variable of the same order: the Yangzi and Huai region is wet in spring and summer and sickness travels easily, and both the expedition of Emperor Taiwu in 450 and that of Tuoba Ying in 478 leave records of sick soldiers and exhaustion, so that the wrong season alone could break an offensive without a battle.
cause: 打起來的原因是多層的疊加。最外層是地理與傳統：自劉宋初年以來，黃河與淮水之間的沃野就是南北爭奪的焦點，誰控制淮北，誰就控制了下游的徵糧與徵兵。直接的前因是劉宋末年的反攻失敗：466年之後，劉宋在彭城、青州一線的北伐接連受挫，淮北之地大部落入北魏之手，南朝退守淮水，此後二十年間兩國的接觸多停在邊境襲擾與示威。474年這一年的特殊性在於南齊內部正在崩壞：後廢帝誅戮將相、朝政暴虐，宮門之內數月數易宰相，蕭道成以整軍的名義不斷擴充中軍與宿衛，朝廷的注意力全在宮中；北魏正是看準這一點，把原本停留在劫掠與示威的邊境衝突，擴大成一場指向壽陽與瓜步的正面攻勢。北方也有自己的理由：魏的軍鎮與屯田在這十年間把河北與中原的存量重新編排，糧源與兵源比太武帝南征時更充裕，這讓長距離南征第一次有可能做成常態，而不是一場孤注一擲的冒險。於是原本零星的邊境戰，在474年之後連續鋪開成連續的攻勢，這就是建康之戰在戰爭史上的位置：它不是一場決戰，而是一次把戰爭升級的嘗試。
causeEn: The reasons were layered. The outermost was geography and precedent: since the early Liu Song, the fertile country between the Yellow River and the Huai had been the point of contention between north and south, and whoever held the north bank controlled the levy of grain and men for the lower reaches. The immediate occasion was the failure of the Liu Song counter-offensives: after 466 the Song thrusts toward Pengcheng and Qingzhou were defeated in turn, most of the country north of the Huai fell to Northern Wei, the southern court withdrew to the river, and for some twenty years afterwards the two states met only in border raiding and display. What made 474 special was the collapse of government inside Southern Qi: the Later Emperor butchered ministers and general officers and his rule was dissolute, chancellors changed hands several times in a few months within the palace gates, while Xiao Daocheng used the pretext of restoring military discipline to expand the Central Army and the guards; the court's whole attention was fixed on the palace. Northern Wei read the situation exactly, converting a border conflict that had amounted to plunder and display into a full offensive aimed at Shouyang and Guabu. The north had its own reasons: the military towns and state farms of Wei had rearranged the resources of the Yellow River and the Central Plains over those ten years, and grain and manpower were more abundant than they had been when Tuoba Tao campaigned south, which for the first time made a long march into the south a routine operation rather than a desperate gamble. Thus the scattered fighting of the border turned, after 474, into a run of continuous offensives, and that is the place of the Battle of Jiankang in the history of the war: it was not a decisive battle, but an attempt to raise the scale of the war.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果，是南北之間那條線從此變得清晰而殘酷。江淮一帶的城池、村落與人口被反覆爭奪，田地一年熟一熟就因為兵而廢，南朝從此再難向北恢復劉宋時代的淮北據點，中原的土地與編戶大批歸入北魏的版籍，魏國的糧源與兵源因此更上一層，北方得以把前線維持在淮水一線並不斷向南試探。齊朝這邊的收穫，是戰爭本身帶來的權力重排：蕭道成靠整軍與實際掌兵在宮中廢掉後廢帝、擁立順帝，最後代宋建齊，齊的立國本身幾乎是這場邊境戰爭的副產品；陳顯達在壽陽、瓜步一線練出的防禦經驗，後來成為南朝對付北魏與北周的基本套路：以城塞換時間、以弩砲換騎兵、以斷糧換時間差。技術層面的影響更長：南北朝在這幾十年裡反覆琢磨怎麼讓步卒在沒有羅馬式重裝備的情況下頂住騎兵衝鋒，於是有了深溝高壘、槊林與弩砲配合的守城法門，也有了齊軍在瓜步江岸設榔這種把水陸兵力合成一段的部署，隋唐在江南與北方作戰時仍在沿用同一套思路。個人層面上，拓跋英在建武年間的病卒讓北魏的南征指揮中斷，齊魏的僵局再沒有被一次大攻勢打破，兩國又維持了將近七十年的相持，直到隋滅陳。
impactEn: The immediate effect of this war was that the line between north and south became at once clear and merciless. The towns, villages and people of the Yangzi and Huai region were fought over again and again, and the fields were abandoned with every harvest because of the soldiers; the southern court could never again recover the bases north of the Huai that the Liu Song had held, and the great mass of the Central Plain's land and registered households passed into Northern Wei's territory, so that Wei's grain and manpower rose another step, letting the north keep the front on the Huai while probing further south again and again. The harvest on the Qi side was a rearrangement of power produced by the war itself: Xiao Daocheng used the army and the actual command of troops to depose the Later Emperor inside the palace, set up Prince Zhun, and finally replaced the Song and founded Southern Qi, so that the founding of the dynasty was very nearly a by-product of this border war. The defensive experience Chen Xianda built at Shouyang and Guabu became the standard southern method against Wei and then against Northern Zhou: trade time for fortified towns, trade crossbows for cavalry, trade a cut grain road for a gap in time. The technical influence was longer lasting: for several decades north and south turned over and over the question of how infantry could stand against a cavalry charge without Roman-style heavy equipment, and so arose the method of deep ditches and high works with spear-forests and crossbows working together, and also deployments such as the stockades along the riverbank at Guabu that fused water and land forces into a single line, an approach the Sui and Tang still used in their fighting in the south and the north. At the personal level, the death of Tuoba Ying during the Jianwu years cut the northern command of the southern campaigns, and the Qi-Wei stalemate was never again broken by a single great offensive; the two states went on maintaining the standoff for close to seventy years, until the Sui destroyed the Chen.
result: 打到最後，魏軍沒有過江，建康沒有陷落。瓜步壘與江岸的設榔把北魏的騎兵擋在水面之外，壽陽一線的攻城也因為南方援軍不斷抵達而無法速下，魏軍在缺糧、多雨與疫病之間熬了數月，最後只能整隊退回淮北。這一輪攻勢的收束是在479年：南齊由陳顯達出兵收復壽陽，把前線重新推到淮水南岸；同一年蕭道成受禪稱帝，南宋至此變成南齊，齊魏之間的戰線也就此固定下來，長江以南與淮水以北的南北分界在接下來的近七十年裡再沒有被打破。對南朝來說，這是一場守住家的戰爭：首都沒有失守，前線雖然丟了壽陽，卻換來了三年時間去整頓朝政、建立新朝的班底與重新編排將領。對北魏來說，這是一場沒有勝負的攻勢：淮南的城池到手了，卻沒有渡過長江，遠征的成本仍然要從屯田與軍鎮的收成裡一點一點償還。用卡面這件兵器來收尾最為恰當：羅馬重步兵從來不是靠一身重甲贏的，靠的是後方能持續補上兵源與糧食；這場戰爭裡雙方爭的其實是同一件事，只是南北朝沒有羅馬的兵役制度與道路，只能用更笨的辦法，把人和糧一船一船、一車一車搬到前線去。
resultEn: In the end the Wei army did not cross the river, and Jiankang did not fall. The redoubt at Guabu and the stockades along the bank held the Wei cavalry off the water; the siege of Shouyang could not be brought to a quick decision because relief from the south kept arriving, and the Wei host, short of grain and worn by rain and sickness, endured for months before withdrawing in order to the north of the Huai. The round was closed in 479, when Southern Qi sent Chen Xianda to retake Shouyang and pushed the front back to the south bank of the Huai; in the same year Xiao Daocheng received the abdication and became emperor, the Song became Southern Qi, and the line between the two states was fixed, the division between the lands south of the Yangzi and north of the Huai not being broken again in the nearly seventy years that followed. For the southern court this was a war to hold the house: the capital was safe, the front lost Shouyang, but it bought three years in which to reform the government, lay the foundations of the new dynasty and reshuffle its commanders. For Northern Wei it was an offensive with no decision: the cities of the Huai were taken, yet the Yangzi was not crossed, and the cost of the campaign still had to be repaid out of the returns of the state farms and the military towns. The weapon on the card is the best way to close. A Roman legionary was never won by heavy armour but by a rear that could keep supplying men and grain, and what the two sides were really fighting for in 474 was the same thing; only the Southern and Northern Dynasties had no Roman system of service and no roads, so they had to do it the slow way, moving men and grain forward by boat and by cart.
